2.tense: You will be gripping the whole pattern as if the choice could be secured before it happens.
2.verb: Directing attention toward what you choose
2.place: Standing outside the system, inside it, seeing what's true across every layer
2.ask: Sketch the arrangement you're bracing inside right now, with your own place on it. Put the other people and pressures down as they actually sit. Change nothing on the page.
2.core:
Here the same thing is running ahead of itself. The direction is real, but it's reaching for a future nobody can write in yet, and the whole picture gets squeezed into a plan. What settled you turns white-knuckled: the choice already made, the outcome already required, the layers pressed flat so nothing can surprise you. From outside it looks like conviction. From inside it feels like holding a door shut.

What loosens it isn't a lighter grip on nothing. It's seeing more of the shape. Put the whole arrangement on paper, yourself included where you actually stand in it. You already read across the layers; do that here, on this one. The pattern isn't finished, and that itself is information. What you're forcing wants to be known, not decided. Seeing it fully, without closing the case, hands the choice back to now.
2.sheetLine: You're gripping the outcome before it's happened.

3.tense: You had been reading the whole pattern, and now you stand at a door that closed behind you.
3.verb: Directing attention toward what you choose
3.place: Standing outside the system, inside it, seeing what's true across every layer
3.ask: Do one ordinary task this week at your own pace, in your own order, and don't trim it down. Notice afterward that part of it came from you.
3.core:
There's a way of seeing what's true across a whole situation that has stepped back here. Not because the skill is gone. The pattern is right there, and the person who could read it is off to the side, so choices arrive as though circumstance made them. What's the point, the week says. That's where things stand, and it doesn't need a reason from you.

Pushing at the pattern won't open it. Effort aimed at the whole thing lands nowhere. What opens it is smaller and closer to you: being what you already are in one plain act. One task at your own pace, in your own order, unproved and untrimmed. That's not a demonstration of will. It's ordinary proof that part of what you do still comes from you, and the reading starts again there.
3.sheetLine: The pattern is clear and you've stopped reading it.

4.tense: The pattern is being read and acted on right now, and the hand holding it says it merely keeps up.
4.verb: Directing attention toward what you choose
4.place: Standing outside the system, inside it, seeing what's true across every layer
4.ask: Take something you did this week you'd call just responding, and say what you chose in it, in one sentence. Read that sentence back to yourself.
4.core:
Direction is happening. Something is choosing which layers to look at, which move comes next, and the account given is that you're keeping up with what the week demanded. The pattern gets read, the choice gets made, and the credit goes to momentum or habit or the situation. Some of that account is accurate. But the hand making the choices is present, and it has been describing itself as the circumstances'.

The correction runs smaller, not larger, back toward what's plainly yours. Take one ordinary act and put into a sentence what you chose in it. Not a case for yourself, just the accurate trace. You'll be looking at the point where a choice entered without being noticed as one. Your name on what you already did is where doing it on purpose begins.
4.sheetLine: It's yours already, you've just been calling it momentum.

1.tense: Right now the person is choosing a direction and meaning it, one thing at a time.
1.verb: Steering by a chosen direction, saying this and not that
1.place: At the point where what has been gathered is complete enough to set down and leave from
1.ask: Take what you're already carrying through this stretch and hold it the way you'd hold something that's already yours — no tighter than it needs. When it's done, the work finishes by itself.
1.core:
You can pick a direction and hold it without forcing anything. When several things pull at once, you say this one, not those, and the choice settles you instead of winding you up. What you're steering stays yours, and you stay in the middle of it rather than ahead of it.

What keeps this working is bearing the weight without stiffening under it. Take the task or situation you're already carrying and carry it without making your grip harder than the thing requires. Let the stretch finish without you managing the finish. Fortitude here isn't endurance as grimness — it's a hand that stays soft while it holds. Loosen when the work is done, and the ease comes back by itself.
1.sheetLine: You choose the direction and hold it without hardening around it.

2.tense: Ahead of now, the person is forcing how everything will turn out before anything has happened.
2.verb: Steering by a chosen direction, saying this and not that
2.place: At the point where what has been gathered is complete enough to set down and leave from
2.ask: Take the situation you're trying to force and draw the whole arrangement on one page — everything in it, and where you stand in it. Look at the page instead of fixing it.
2.core:
There's a direction in you, and lately it's been aimed at outcomes that haven't happened yet. Every branch gets decided in advance, every person's move gets anticipated, and you push to make the future arrive on schedule. It doesn't, and the pushing gets harder.

What untightens this is seeing the whole arrangement you're standing inside instead of the next thing to force. Put it on a page — who's in it, what's actually happening, where you are — and look without correcting. The pattern shows you more than the next move will. Recognition doesn't close the question; it just moves your eyes off the wheel for a minute, which is where the grip loosens.
2.sheetLine: You're forcing a future that hasn't agreed to anything yet.

3.tense: The person is still standing at a door that closed behind them, and nothing has moved since.
3.verb: Steering by a chosen direction, saying this and not that
3.place: At the point where what has been gathered is complete enough to set down and leave from
3.ask: Choose an ordinary task and do it your way, not the correct way — your pace, your order, your shape — and don't account for the choice to anyone.
3.core:
Direction isn't moving here. The days pass and you're not steering; you're being carried, and no choice has felt like it changed anything in a long time. Passivity looks like the sensible response to a door that already shut.

But nothing has to be corrected in you to start again. Pick an ordinary task and do it your own way — your pace, your order, your shape — and don't explain the choice. That isn't a performance of who you are; it's simply you doing a thing the way only you would. Radiance without ego is the shape of it: shining because it's what you are, not to make a point. One task handled like that and the steering comes back through the same door it left.
3.sheetLine: You stopped choosing and called it what's the point.

4.tense: The person is steering right now and telling it as something that simply happened.
4.verb: Steering by a chosen direction, saying this and not that
4.place: At the point where what has been gathered is complete enough to set down and leave from
4.ask: Find a decision you've been calling circumstance or good timing, and treat it as a decision you made. No announcement, no ceremony — just let it be yours.
4.core:
Your life has a direction and it's been holding steady through a lot. You talk about it as the current — things came together, the timing worked, it went that way. But somebody kept picking on the way here, and it was you.

Start smaller than feels right. There's one decision you've been filing under luck or circumstance; begin treating it as something you chose, and stop there. No audience, no ceremony. What you already are is already written down — your name is just missing from one of the pages. Being what you are here is quieter than claiming it, which is why it slides past you so easily.
4.sheetLine: You chose it, and you've been telling it as something that happened.
